teaching.causalExplanation: When magnesium burns, magnesium plus oxygen gives magnesium oxide. Magnesium oxide is ionic, so each magnesium atom has become a magnesium ion by losing two electrons, and each oxygen atom has gained two, becoming an oxide ion. So the real change in burning isn't the oxygen itself. It's electrons moving from one atom to another. So chemists widened the words. Oxidation is the loss of electrons. Reduction is the gain of electrons. To remember it, think oil rig. Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain. In our beaker, zinc loses electrons, so zinc is oxidised. Copper ions gain electrons, so copper ions are reduced. And the old meaning still fits, because magnesium loses electrons to oxygen, so it's oxidised too. Electrons can't just vanish. So whenever one substance loses electrons, another has to gain them. Oxidation and reduction always happen together, and a reaction with both is called a redox reaction, short for reduction and oxidation. So whenever you spot an oxidation, look for the reduction that goes with it.

1. Oxidation: loss of electrons. Reduction: gain of electrons.
